title: Rank Athena self-fix requests ahead of feature work in plan and drain
summary: Within the same effective priority tier, plan and drain order requests that fix Athena itself (steward or Hestia root-cause, repeated-failure, blind-spot and gate-review items) before feature and content items. Steward website and study content requests do not count as fixes. Goal: the steward's filed requests stop starving behind older feature items. Audience: the owner, who runs `athena plan` and `athena drain`.

defaults_applied.how: New unit and drain tests; cargo test and clippy must pass.
Criteria check the plan order and the dispatch order, not that a field exists.
The sort key in Plan::build_with is changed, not individual items re-prioritised.
The rule is enforced in the sort key and covered by tests.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Code survey: crates/athena-core/src/plan.rs (Plan::build_with picks the ready items with the best effective priority, then sorts them by `(e.rung, age)` at about line 783; PlanEntry struct and PlanEntry::bare; module doc 'Order' paragraph; proposal_priority), crates/athena-core/src/reading/topics.rs (plan_entry builds entries from JobRecords), crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs (around line 4340 builds the entry and finds the approved work item through work_decisions::decision_of; calls proposal_priority), crates/athena-data/src/records/work.rs (WorkItem has role, kind BlindSpot|RepeatedFailure|Proposal, key, title, source; WorkItemKind). The entry point is `athena plan` / `athena drain` calling Plan::build_with. No new record or data file is added under crates/, so check_record_file, AnyRecord and the round-trip test are untouched; any new PlanEntry field is serde-skipped when false so existing serialized plans are unchanged. Order is measured directly by the plan order vector in unit tests, not through a stand-in.
Term ladder: 'tier' means a priority level (urgent, high, normal, low); 'rung' means the requirement ladder rung used as the second sort key in Plan::build_with.

Interpretation: a request is a fix when it comes from an approved work item whose role is the steward or Hestia and whose kind is BlindSpot or RepeatedFailure, or whose key or title marks a root-cause or gate-review fix. A steward Proposal that touches only website or studies/ content is not a fix. The new key is applied only inside the best effective priority tier, so an explicit priority record, Priority: line or urgent/high cap always wins over it. Fix items sort by (not-fix, rung, age), so rung then age order is preserved within each group.

Docs: the 'Order' paragraph in the plan.rs module doc is updated. A decision recording the new rule is appended to docs/decisions.md as a new entry with a Provenance bullet; no existing entry is edited. athena.toml, defaults.toml and workflows are not changed (Consumers: none found).
Previous-result check: no earlier job is named in the request, so there is nothing to keep or exclude.

acceptance_criteria.text: A new unit test in crates/athena-core/src/plan.rs builds a plan with an older normal feature entry and a newer normal fix entry that are both ready; the plan order puts the fix entry first. Check by running `cargo test -p athena-core`.

A unit test shows an urgent or high feature item still comes before a normal fix item, and an item that depends on another still comes after it, so the fix flag never overrides priority or dependencies. Check by running `cargo test -p athena-core`.

A unit test shows a steward request for website or studies content is not flagged as a fix and keeps its age-ordered place behind older items of the same tier. Check by running `cargo test -p athena-cli`.

A drain test in crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs (or a unit test in crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs) has an approved steward blind-spot or repeated-failure work item and an older feature request, both normal priority. The drain dispatches the steward job first. Check by running `cargo test -p athena-cli`.

The plan.rs module doc 'Order' paragraph describes the fix-first rule as applying inside a priority tier. The diff shows Plan::build_with changing the `ready.sort_by_key` key to place fix entries before others.
docs/decisions.md gains a new appended entry stating the rule, with a Provenance bullet citing the owner's request. No existing entry changes. CHANGELOG.md records the job.
`cargo test`, `cargo clippy` and `cargo fmt --check` pass on the final tree, using Athena's recorded checks on the same tree.

out_of_scope: Changing how steward or Hestia raise or classify work items
Changing priority levels, urgent/high caps, or the `athena priority` command
Editing existing entries in docs/decisions.md or anything under records/
Changes to athena.toml, defaults.toml or CI workflows
departures: The change reaches both the core plan order and the CLI drain entry builder, with tests in two crates, so cost and time are slightly above the reference.
hard_reason: Changes the ordering rule that decides which requests the plan and drain run first, so a mistake would be costly and hard to see.
